correctness.rationale: All quantifiers are explicit: simple cycles of orders m,n>=3; for 5<=m<=n the n C_m-fibers require at least three selected vertices each by the cited Cartesian-fiber criterion. For each nonexceptional pair, the explicit floor-stretching construction uses exactly three vertices per column, each a rotation of the cycle-monitoring triple. The selected columns for a fixed row are unions of fibers of the nondecreasing surjection floor(mj/n); consecutive selected column blocks have circular gaps bounded by ceil(floor((m-1)/3)*n/m)+1. This is strictly less than n/2 when n>=13, or when 5<=m<=n<=12 except (5,6),(7,8). The two exceptional arrays have column and row circular gaps strictly less than half the relevant cycle lengths. The C_3,C_4 cases follow because each of those factors requires all vertices. The proof is infinite and does not infer anything infinite from finite experiments. The standalone program independently checks all 36 small arithmetic cases, 7491 explicit construction parameters, and each edge-deletion monitoring condition directly on 14 small product graphs (1318 edges), all passed, with 16 additional direct checks for short-cycle factors. No unproved external lemma beyond the cited, directly inspected Cartesian-fiber characterization and elementary cycle facts is required.

originality.rationale: Haslegrave's Theorem 4 establishes the square Cartesian torus only, meg(C_m square C_m)=3m. His Theorem 1 establishes a lower bound max(3m,3n) for two cycles and an upper bound 3m+3n-9. When m!=n>=5 these bounds differ, so that theorem by itself does not imply their equality. The new contribution explicitly attains the lower bound for every unequal aspect ratio, using a balanced staircase retraction and two exceptional tables. The founding paper classifies cycles and ordinary grid families but not rectangular toroidal products. The closely titled product-network article's accessible abstract identifies other product operations and does not state the new formula; its full text was unavailable for a conclusive comparison. Literature and published-record searches found no equivalent result, which cannot prove publication priority. The prior square case and known small-cycle cases are credited rather than recast as new.
residual_risks: The full text of the 2024 product-networks article was not accessible for a conclusive negative comparison; abstract-level scope does not establish noncoverage.

The science has no independent mathematical audit or external priority certification.

value.rationale: This closes a natural two-parameter exact invariant classification in an established graph-product monitoring problem. Prior research explicitly highlights the square torus as a case where the Cartesian lower bound is attained; the rectangular theorem shows this persists without any aspect-ratio penalty. Its discrete floor-stretching layout supplies an explicit optimal sensor choice for every size, including two genuine short-aspect exceptional adjustments. This is a complete structural extension, not a cosmetic change of the already known square formula, and it distinguishes rectangular toroidal grids from path products where the opposite bound is attained.
